key_facts: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quit as chief executive after reports of alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, Alice Huang (no relation), who worked at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed; a second reported relationship was with long-time Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell.

Nvidia lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in five days; the stock fell 31% from its recent peak, the largest five-day drop since the company went public 27 years ago. Nvidia's value is about 7% of the S&P 500.

CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO; Nvidia is searching for a permanent replacement. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department had not yet drawn conclusions on whether Alice Huang engaged in espionage for Beijing; China rejected the allegations as a smear. Senators Warren and Coons and House Democrats demanded Huang brief Congress.
importance_reason: Leadership exit at one of the world's most valuable AI chipmakers with a $550bn five-day market-cap loss and a national-security dimension, though the underlying espionage claims remain unconfirmed.
market_link: Sharp drop in Nvidia shares affects AI-sector valuations and, via its ~7% weight, the S&P 500 and US index-fund retirement accounts; leadership uncertainty may weigh on the chip supply chain and AI-related equities.

key_facts: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reportedly took a softer line on Nvidia's advanced AI chip sales than other senior Trump administration officials, who broadly favor tighter controls to keep China from using the chips in the AI race.

Over the past year, Lutnick has frequently clashed with top officials over how to regulate advanced technology sales, particularly Nvidia's chip sales to Asia; critics in the administration and Congress say the Commerce Department is too cozy with Nvidia and co-founder Jensen Huang and has not adequately policed chip sales to China.

The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang was in a relationship with Alice Huang, a top executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China; U.S. intelligence agencies reportedly believe she is a Chinese spy. Jensen Huang announced he was stepping down from Megaspeed, and the company's shares fell sharply.

Lutnick, as head of the department that enforces technology sales restrictions, is positioned to largely shape whether China gets access to American technology; within Commerce, Nvidia reportedly receives different treatment, with its issues given high priority and routed through specific channels.
importance_reason: Значимый политико-регуляторный сюжет о контроле экспорта AI-чипов в Китай с заметным корпоративным эффектом, но без немедленного решения или количественного рыночного шока.
market_link: Экспортные ограничения на Nvidia-чипы и возможные новые меры против Megaspeed могут влиять на акции Nvidia и полупроводникового сектора, а также на ожидания по доступу китайских компаний к AI-оборудованию.

key_facts: Microsoft says it is working to tackle "connectivity problems" after users worldwide reported outages on Thursday; services including Teams, Outlook and Copilot were affected.

Microsoft said a part of its infrastructure was experiencing "elevated load", likely contributing to connectivity errors; the issue was first reported in the US, but could affect users "in any region".
Downdetector showed over 131,000 reports of Microsoft Outlook problems in the US at 18:15 GMT; a spike in UK user reports was also seen around 18:30 GMT.
In an update at 19:50 GMT, Microsoft said it was "testing a configuration" to fix the problem, which was causing servers to fail automated health checks; all affected servers had been restarted.
importance_reason: Временный технический сбой у крупного провайдера без подтверждённого рыночного эффекта.

key_facts: Estate agents in the UK increasingly use AI to enhance property listing photos (repainted walls, added lawns, furniture, decluttering), a practice critics call 'housefishing'. One in five of 906 surveyed UK homebuyers who purchased in the past year said they had viewed a property with digitally enhanced listing photos that made it look better than it was.

Olivia Nicole (29) found a five-bedroom London property on Rightmove, Zoopla and Winkworth whose AI-enhanced photos showed smaller windows, different decor, and a wall structure absent in the images; the three companies said they had strict AI guidelines and removed the images. Jack Bushrod reported a 'surge' of AI-enhanced listings over six months, including one image where a pillar was removed and a window added.

Trading Standards says agents may use AI for basic enhancements or virtual furnishing if disclosed, but structurally altering rooms or hiding features may mislead consumers and break the law. Howards (Lowestoft) said it now labels all AI-enhanced photos and does not use AI to misrepresent a property's fundamental features.
importance_reason: Consumer-protection and housing-market practice story with limited direct market impact; no macro or asset-price effect identified in the source.

key_facts: Stripe is positioning itself as a key component ("cog") for agentic commerce, in which AI bots make purchases using credit cards.
JPMorgan Chase is described as a skeptic of agentic commerce.
Banks are racing to keep up with the development of AI bots using credit cards, according to the headline.
importance_reason: Отраслевая новость о платёжной инфраструктуре без макро- или рыночного эффекта; текст ограничен лидом.
